name: Day One
tagline: Private journal with media, location, prompts, and cross-device sync

pricing.notes: Official pricing page reviewed; taxes, promotions, and regional pricing may differ.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited text entries and journals; 1 device; 1 photo/entry; web access, shared journals and exports

tiers.name: Silver
tiers.limits: Unlimited devices; up to 30 photos/videos per entry; audio/transcription, PDF scans, integrations; 25% print discount

tiers.name: Gold
tiers.limits: Silver plus reflective AI, daily chat, prompts/summaries/title suggestions/image generation; 35% print discount

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited text entries and journals; 1 device; 1 photo per entry
pricing.billingTerms: annual only for Silver and Gold; 1-month in-app trial; no public monthly plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Gold AI has daily fair-use limits, but Day One does not publish the numbers. Trial eligibility and billing changes are controlled by the original app-store platform.

verdictSummary: The visible digital journal loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Day One earns its keep through polish, sync, importers, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local-first digital journal app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Day One: People pay for a writing surface they trust for years, plus migration tools, sync, and tiny interaction details that disappear into habit.
ongoingBurden: Own schema migrations, backups, sync conflicts, export compatibility, and long-term file readability.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Day One is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Day One, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local-first digital journal app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: conflict-safe multi-device sync; mature importers and exporters; collaborative editing and sharing.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
